source: AlphaPROBE: Alpha Mining via Principled Retrieval and On-graph Biased Evolution
title: R33 Factor Mining: Add AlphaPROBE as third framework alongside QuantaAlpha and FactorMiner
rationale: AlphaPROBE (Feb 2026, github.com/gta0804/AlphaPROBE) introduces a complementary approach to factor mining via DAG navigation. While QuantaAlpha (already staged) uses evolutionary trajectory optimization and FactorMiner uses skill+experience memory pools, AlphaPROBE uniquely models the entire factor lineage as a Directed Acyclic Graph and uses a Bayesian Factor Retriever that penalizes over-explored branches. IC scores on Chinese markets: 5.84/6.26/9.04 for CSI300/500/1000. Sharpe ratios: 0.44/0.83/0.65. The Bayesian retriever prevents the redundancy problem we've seen in naive evolutionary search by tracking how many times a parent node has been retrieved and reducing its selection probability — directly addressing the 'what-failed exclusion pool' lesson from FactorMiner heuristics. The key additive value vs QuantaAlpha: AlphaPROBE's ancestral-aware generation prevents producing near-duplicates of existing factors in the pool, which QuantaAlpha's crossover+mutation can accidentally do.
content:
## AI Research Findings (Dream Cycle 2026-04-20)

### AlphaPROBE: DAG-Based Factor Mining (arXiv:2602.11917, Feb 2026)
- Models factor pool as a Directed Acyclic Graph; navigation via Bayesian Factor Retriever + DAG-aware Generator
- Bayesian retriever balances exploitation vs over-optimization: prior = quality × (1-γ)^depth × (1-ω)^n_retrievals (penalizes frequently-mined branches)
- IC: 5.84%/6.26%/9.04% on CSI300/500/1000; Sharpe 0.44/0.83/0.65; outperforms AlphaAgent, R&D-Agent(Q)
- Key advantage vs QuantaAlpha: ancestral awareness prevents near-duplicate factor generation (QuantaAlpha crossover can accidentally regenerate near-duplicates without lineage awareness)
- LLM backbone: Deepseek V3.1; embedding: Qwen 3 Embedding; pool cap: 50 factors; code: https://github.com/gta0804/AlphaPROBE (Apache 2.0)
- R33 application: run AlphaPROBE in parallel with QuantaAlpha; each generates different factor candidates; combine pools via diversity filter (|corr| < 0.70, ranked by RankIC desc)

### EvasionBench + Eva-4B: Purpose-Built Evasion Classifier (arXiv:2601.09142, Jan 2026)
- Eva-4B (HuggingFace: FutureMa/Eva-4B-V2, Apache 2.0, 4B params, Qwen3-4B base): 84.9% Macro-F1, outperforms Claude Opus 4.5, GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Flash on evasion detection
- 3-class taxonomy: direct / intermediate / fully_evasive. Per-class F1: Direct 0.851, Intermediate 0.698, Fully_Evasive 0.873
- Quantified market impact: +40pp evasion → -0.74% 1-day return; 63% underperformance probability within 180 days
- R28 amendment: replace ad-hoc 3-step NOR LLM prompt with Eva-4B inference. NOR_rate = (intermediate + fully_evasive) / total Q&A pairs
- NUANCE vs prior heuristic (arXiv:2505.18419): moderate evasion (25-50%) = PEAD amplifier (information asymmetry); extreme evasion (>50%) = BEARISH veto (hiding bad news). The two thresholds produce different signals.
- GitHub: IIIIQIIII/EvasionBench (inference scripts in /scripts, Colab notebook); dataset: FutureMa/EvasionBench (16.7K labeled Q&A pairs, Parquet)

### Acoustic Camouflage (arXiv:2604.14619, April 2026) — NEGATIVE FINDING
- Adding acoustic/prosodic features to earnings call NLP models HURTS performance: recall drops from 66.25% to 47.08%
- Root cause: executives use media training to suppress natural vocal stress indicators (pitch, rate, energy do not reveal stress for trained speakers)
- DO NOT add audio features to any earnings call pipeline. NLP-only is strictly superior for this domain.
